title: Pause sessions for maintenance
goal: Ask connected browsers to save and pause before stopping the server.

selectionNotes: Persist state; same document/retention/keys. Acceptance is not drain; request cancellation does not guarantee shutdown.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: The newer automatic/server-directed pause APIs are ASP.NET Core 11.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Build net11.0 with matching Web SDK, Razor and browser assets.

language.name: C#
language.reason: Canonical language mode; these APIs need no C# 15-specific syntax.

prerequisites: Use the Web SDK, AddRazorComponents/AddInteractiveServerComponents, AddInteractiveServerRenderMode, MapStaticAssets and the matching blazor.web.js. No additional workload or external account is needed.

Persist the needed JSON-serializable component properties with [PersistentState], initialize defaults in OnInitialized, and retain stable component identity. Component trees, scoped resources, file inputs and arbitrary object graphs are not hibernated.

The default provider is local in-memory circuit persistence (1,000 circuits/two hours). Resume in the same loaded document within retention; no full refresh. Restart recovery also needs the protected state received by the browser and the same compatible app/component identities and Data Protection keys. Distributed/multi-instance storage and key sharing require separate design and proof.

Track connected circuits with a CircuitHandler. Begin maintenance before the transport is torn down, close admission, snapshot the sessions and request pause from actual host lifecycle code. Keep the server available while observing closure within a bounded host shutdown budget.
constraints: Interactive Server; cancellation of request is not guaranteed completed shutdown.
Persisted state is a recoverable draft, not durable business storage. Scope disposal and a new circuit/resource identity prove release; a still-visible DOM snapshot does not.

Task<bool> reports whether the framework accepted and asked the client to pause. false covers an unavailable/disconnected circuit or cancellation before acceptance; it does not mean all sessions stopped. Observe OnConnectionDownAsync and OnCircuitClosedAsync; a client can defer and the budget can expire.

The local successful maintenance proof uses WebApplication.StopAsync, reaching StoppingAsync before transport shutdown. Calling StopApplication first raced the connection in a negative run: true acceptance but no completed drain. Do proactive maintenance while serving, and do not promise graceful capture for termination signals, abrupt kills or canceled budgets.

A resumed circuit recreates scoped services; persist service values only with an appropriate RegisterPersistentService registration. Never persist live handles or assume a disposed service instance returns.

The .NET 10 app-owned visibility/JS bridge is a verified previous-release comparison, not a .NET 10 route for the new APIs. Static SSR, WebAssembly, Interactive Auto, distributed failover, mobile lifecycle and GA behavior are not execution claims.
